theme: AirDNA / Mashvisor / AllTheRooms / Transparent / Key Data / Rabbu / Awning sample exports or scraped market pages committed to GitHub
queries_run: gh search repos "airdna market data" --sort stars
gh search repos "short-term rental occupancy csv" --sort stars
notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: AirDNA, Mashvisor, Key Data, Transparent, Rabbu, and Awning all gate their market data behind paid subscriptions/APIs with terms of service that forbid redistribution, so almost nothing found is a real committed dataset -- most hits are (a) job-interview/take-home coding exercises that reference these vendors by name but ship no vendor data, (b) thin API-client wrappers requiring a paid key, or (c) unrelated name collisions (a Swedish airborne-eDNA study called 'AirDNA_Size_Fractions'; dozens of GitHub users literally named Rabbu/Rabbul -- 'rabbu' as a keyword is mostly useless, all hits excluded as noise). 'Transparent' and 'Awning' returned zero repos on any phrasing tried -- likely too generic a word to search or genuinely no GitHub footprint. Two scraper repos (airdna site itself, not airbnb.com) are catalogued per the rules as methods, unrun. TimKahn/Guess_the_Address is the closest to a real research use of AirDNA data (Denver STR/VRBO fuzzy-matching project) but the repo's own .gitignore and lack of a data/ folder indicate the proprietary AirDNA/VRBO CSVs were NOT committed -- code only. Net: this pass found no material dataset for gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from a free source); that gap likely stays open unless a scout on 'academic paper + AirDNA' or 'Zenodo AirDNA replication' phrasing (not tried here, worth another scout's time) turns up a replication package with the underlying export attached as supplementary data. Also worth another scout: Wayback Machine captures of AirDNA/Mashvisor/Rabbu public market-data pages (gap #17) -- not searched here since it is GH-search-only and Wayback tooling repos didn't surface under these keywords.

candidates.name: Guess_the_Address
candidates.what_it_holds: Metis data-science capstone (7 stars, last active 2025). Uses 'AirDNA proprietary data' for Denver (avg. 833 properties within 500m circles around listings), VRBO/HomeAway data scraped/provided by AirDNA, and Denver Tax Assessor records, fuzzy-matched to ~429 linked records; goal is predicting a listing's true street address from AirDNA-anonymized data. Repo root has README, model/, munge/, scrape/, visualize/ folders but NO data/ directory and a .gitignore -- the underlying AirDNA/VRBO CSVs are not committed, confirmed via `gh api contents/`. Entire-home Denver listings only.
candidates.why_useful: Documents concretely what an AirDNA Denver export contains (fields, granularity, ~833-listing single-market size) and a working method (fuzzy match to tax-assessor records) for de-anonymizing/cross-referencing STR data, but ships no reusable data -- addresses gap #2 only as a description of the shape of AirDNA data, not as a source.
candidates.size_hint: no data files committed; code only

candidates.name: rental-averages
candidates.what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed app (2023) that 'processes data from AirDNA to output a mean average of occupancy and ADR.' README does not show a committed sample CSV; appears to be a calculator/processor expecting the user to supply their own AirDNA export.
candidates.why_useful: Shows the exact metric pairing (occupancy + ADR) AirDNA exports carry and a ready-made aggregation method, but no data of its own -- would only help if paired with an actual export.
candidates.size_hint: code only, no data files evident

candidates.name: airdnascraper
candidates.what_it_holds: 2 stars, active as recently as Jan 2026. A scraper targeting AirDNA's own site (not airbnb.com) -- exact scope/output not confirmed beyond the repo name and star count; not fetched in depth to conserve budget.
candidates.why_useful: A scraper of AirDNA's public market pages (rather than a paid-API client) would be the most direct route to realised ADR/occupancy proxies (gap #2) if AirDNA's site still exposes free market-level stats; scraping AirDNA (a non-Airbnb site) is explicitly in scope per our rules as a catalogued, unrun method.

candidates.name: airdna-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Another scraper named for AirDNA's site, updated Feb 2026; contents not inspected in depth.
candidates.why_useful: Same rationale as jayesh2278/airdnascraper -- a method for pulling AirDNA public market pages, catalogued unrun.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possible duplicate of jayesh2278/airdnascraper in scope/intent

candidates.name: airdna-property-manager-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Sep 2026 repo; scrapes AirDNA's property-manager directory/listings rather than market ADR/occupancy stats (based on name only, not fetched in depth).
candidates.why_useful: Likely a lead-gen tool (property manager contact scraping) rather than market-metric data; flagged for completeness but probably off-target for KPI forecasting.

candidates.name: airdna-api
candidates.what_it_holds: 2-star client library for AirDNA's official (paid) Enterprise API, maintained by a property-management SaaS (GuestReady). No data committed, requires a paid API key to use.
candidates.why_useful: A ready client if the team ever obtained a paid AirDNA API key; not usable without one. Documents the API's method surface.

candidates.name: airdna-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: FastMCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping AirDNA's paid STR market-data API for use by LLM agents, updated Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Same limitation as guestready/airdna-api -- a method, not data, and needs a paid key.

candidates.name: airdna (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: An 'independent third-party profile of a public API surface' -- documentation/OpenAPI-style mapping of AirDNA's Enterprise API (market metrics, STR listing data, comps, Rentalizer revenue estimates), maintained by the api-evangelist project which catalogues many commercial APIs this way. No AirDNA data itself, just a schema description.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only as a map of what fields/endpoints AirDNA's paid API exposes, in case the team pursues a trial/paid key later; no data to pull today.

candidates.name: mashvisor (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Same api-evangelist style profile, but for Mashvisor's Data API (US STR + LTR + MLS analytics). Documentation only, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Schema reference only; Mashvisor's real API is paid.

candidates.name: mashvisor-api-docs
candidates.what_it_holds: Mashvisor's own official API documentation repo (MIT licensed), pointing to their live paid API for US property/STR/LTR analytics. No sample data files.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Mashvisor has no free data tier; only useful if the team later pays for API access.

candidates.name: stalker-challenge
candidates.what_it_holds: A candidate's solution to AllTheRooms' old public data-science hiring challenge (alltherooms.github.io/hiring/challenge/stalker-challenge.html). The challenge itself supplies NO AllTheRooms/STR data -- it directs solvers to Stanford SNAP's public Gowalla check-in dataset (https://snap.stanford.edu/data/loc-gowalla.html) to compute pairwise 'stalker scores' between users from geotagged check-ins.
candidates.why_useful: Not an STR-vendor dataset at all, but the Gowalla check-in dataset it points to is directly named in CONTEXT.md gap #20 (geotagged tourism/check-in datasets for party-size/group-travel/cross-border proxies) -- worth noting as a rediscovery path to that Stanford dataset via a real-estate-tech hiring challenge, and evidence AllTheRooms itself does not expose free market data even for recruiting purposes.
candidates.size_hint: Gowalla external dataset: ~6.4M check-ins (per SNAP listing, not re-verified here)

candidates.name: airbnb-data-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: A pay-per-use commercial scraper explicitly marketed as 'a pay-per-use AirDNA alternative' -- scrapes airbnb.com listings, prices, availability, occupancy, ADR/RevPAR and reviews to JSON/CSV. Updated Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets airbnb.com itself, not a third-party vendor, so it falls under the repo's rule 6 (any scraping of airbnb.com beyond the sanctioned Inside Airbnb / fee-panel captures is a ToS decision for a human) -- flagged only for completeness/awareness, not recommended to run.
